tag_legend.canon: Appears in the books per the ledger (wiki-sourced; nothing here was checked against the novels, see ledger section 0).
tag_legend.inspired: House-game extension. ledger_rows then name the nearest canon basis only.
tag_legend.unverified: Claimed as canon but the ledger row is UNVERIFIED (single fan-site claim) or the claim is thin.

confidence_legend: Copied from the ledger Confidence column (VERIFIED / WIKI-ONLY / UNVERIFIED); several rows -> weakest label. null = no ledger row (pure house content).
out_of_scope: No CR, levels, difficulty, credits or loot amounts: Syndicate rules/10 and the loot decks own those. table_refs only point at existing deck ids. GM-only spine seeds are deliberately left out.
how_to_use: Pick canon entries for flavor and staging; house zones list the canon basis for reskinned mobs. announcement.quote is a ledger-row quote (25 words or fewer) or null; otherwise paraphrase the style.

zones.name: The First Floor (floor-wide rules)
zones.name_note: Canon name: The First Floor. House game wraps it as "The Orientation Pit" (see house zones).
zones.staging: A giant square grid of halls split into neighborhoods; each neighborhood has one local mob type and one boss, and its mobs stop respawning when the boss dies. Stairwells only appear about a day and a half in, and saferooms look like transplanted Earth rest stops.

announcement.style: Cascadia talks like a store manager opening for business; patch notes read as cheerful changelogs that scold Crawlers.

mobs.name: Rat
mobs.what: Small, hissing, poisonous-bite rodents that infest every neighborhood and eat dead Crawlers.

hazards.name: Hallway restroom portals
hazards.what: Mismatched Earth doors that all open onto the user's own stall; early bugs made a second entrant explode or get sucked in until patches fixed them. Use as a one-off early-floor gag, not a standing hazard.

features.name: Saferoom rules
features.what: Boxes open only inside; attackers get teleported away; three-strikes rule on violence/theft; explosives are inert.

features.name: Earth rest-stop saferooms
features.what: Fast-food joints and waiting rooms from Earth, with three wall screens.

features.name: Stairwells
features.what: Appear after the first-day cycle; Borough and City boss arenas always contain one; early descent means stasis until the floor ends.

features.name: Tutorial Guild Hall
features.what: Where the HUD and menus unlock and a guide is assigned.

zones.name: Ball of Swine arena (Borough Boss)
zones.name_note: Canon boss: the Ball of Swine, a.k.a. the Porkchop Express, a Borough Boss. Tier wording disputed once (X-009).
zones.staging: A concentric maze of tunnels with a safe courtyard at the gate. A fused sphere of aristocrats rolls on floor tracks while rising and falling walls steer it at the Crawlers, all staged as a rave. Wedge it in place, break it open, then mop up the dazed Tusklings; the stairwell is in the middle.

announcement.style: A short "you have found a Borough Boss chamber" popup in the usual deadpan.
announcement.quote: So, you’ve stumbled into the chamber of the second-weakest type of boss.

mobs.name: Ball of Swine
mobs.what: Rolling battle formation of fused Tusklings; one attack: roll over you.

mobs.name: Tuskling Knight
mobs.what: Tuxedoed pig-faced aristocrat; weak and unarmed once the ball pops.

mobs.what: Gowned female Tuskling, slightly tougher than a Knight.

mobs.name: Tuskling Dominatrix
mobs.what: Last Tuskling standing; a leader of the formation.
mobs.note: Appears on the wiki page for the Ball; no dedicated ledger quote beyond B-003.

hazards.name: Rolling tracks and shifting walls
hazards.what: Grooves in the floor mark the sphere's path; walls rise and fall to redirect it; loud music hides its approach.

hazards.name: Forcefielded stairwell
hazards.what: The exit sits behind a red forcefield until the boss dies.

features.name: Staging courtyard
features.what: A single gate and a courtyard the Ball will not enter; Crawlers can plan there.

features.name: Wedge weakness
features.what: The sphere fills the tunnel, so a solid angled ramp can pin it.
